candidates.name: EU5 Grand Strategy Academy (Paradox mechanics & nation guides)
candidates.niche: Strategy guides and mechanics explainers for Europa Universalis V and the Paradox grand-strategy ecosystem (EU5 primary, CK3/Stellaris/Victoria 3 as expansion lanes)
candidates.format: 10-20 min scripted mechanics explainers and nation opening guides: own-captured gameplay, map/UI overlays, human-written script with AI or self-recorded narration; evergreen 'how X actually works' framing over patch-chasing
candidates.why_now: EU5 launched 2025-11-04 and its guide ecosystem is still thin versus EU4's 12-year-old library. Beginner-guide videos posted within days of launch pulled 43k-222k views each (YouTube API verified). EU4 still had MORE concurrent players than EU5 as of May 2026 (13,503 vs 9,033 per a Steam community comparison), meaning a large veteran population has not yet migrated — a multi-year stream of 'switching to EU5' learners. Paradox titles are decade-long platforms with DLC waves that reset guide demand repeatedly.

demand_evidence.title: The Complete Beginner's Guide To Europa Universalis 5 (Ludi et Historia)
The Ultimate EU5 Starter Guide for New Players! (Lookas et bella)
demand_evidence.finding: 142,492 views since 2025-11-04 on a 22.8k-sub channel — views ~6x subscriber count indicates search/browse-driven demand, not audience-driven (YouTube API)

Community-tracked comparison: EU5 at 9,033 concurrents vs EU4 at 13,503 on 2026-05-02 — large not-yet-migrated veteran audience (search snippet, not independently verified; player count sites steamcharts/steambase blocked 403 this session)
Players actively asking for EU5 YouTube channel recommendations; only a handful of names (Generalist Gaming, The Red Hawk, Budgetmonk, Laith) surface — thin supply signal (search snippet)

competitor_scan.notes: Created 2019, 99.6M total views. Biggest EU-focused guide channel; proves the ceiling, not a blocker for long-tail nation guides. (channels.list)
ATTAINABILITY PROOF: created 2023-02-28, only 22.8k subs, yet its EU5 starter guide hit 142k views. 6.4M total channel views on 218 videos. (channels.list)
Generalist strategy channel; EU5 beginner video 43k views — mid-tier competition. (channels.list)

candidates.monetization_notes: Grand-strategy audience skews older/male/PC — above-average gaming CPM (inference from audience demographics, not verified). Long-tail search traffic gives guides multi-year AdSense life; Patreon works well in Paradox communities; later lanes: campaign VODs, DLC review sponsorships.
candidates.production_complexity: Medium-high: must actually learn/play EU5 deeply (hundreds of hours of domain knowledge is the moat); per-video production is simple (screen capture + overlays + narration). 100+ video well is trivial: ~30 major nations x openings, ~40 core mechanics, economy/warfare/diplomacy deep-dives, patch/DLC updates.
candidates.risks: Patch churn can invalidate specific guides (mitigate: mechanics-first evergreen framing, version-stamped titles). EU5 concurrents trended down ~22% over 30 days per tracker snippet — if the game underperforms long-term the niche shrinks, though Paradox titles historically grow across years of DLC (inference). Niche ceiling is mid-six-figures subs, not millions.
candidates.originality_defense: All footage self-captured from own gameplay; scripts are original systems analysis and tested strategies. Nothing to compile — this content cannot exist without playing the game. Zero reused-content exposure.

candidates.name: Pharloom Depths (Silksong + lore-rich indie lore documentaries)
candidates.niche: Lore deep-dives and theory videos for Hollow Knight: Silksong, expanding to adjacent lore-dense indies (Rain World, Nine Sols, Blasphemous, Tunic, Animal Well)
candidates.format: 12-25 min narrated lore documentaries: own-captured footage, item-text cross-referencing, map graphics, original theories; human-written script (lore fans punish shallow AI scripts), AI or self voice
candidates.why_now: Silksong (Sept 2025) has sold 7M+ copies plus 'millions more' on Game Pass, and Team Cherry announced the FREE Sea of Sorrow expansion for 2026 — a guaranteed second lore-demand wave on a game whose community norm is years of theorycrafting. Brand-new channels are demonstrably breaking in right now: a channel created 2025-08-27 has 1.9M views in under 11 months.

demand_evidence.finding: Free Sea of Sorrow expansion launching 2026 — scheduled demand-reset event for lore content

demand_evidence.finding: 357,016 views on a video published 2026-02-14 — five months AFTER launch, demand persists (YouTube API)

demand_evidence.title: The Lore Behind All Endings in Silksong (Marushca)
demand_evidence.finding: 237,977 views from a 5,500-subscriber channel — views 43x subs = pure topic demand (YouTube API)

competitor_scan.notes: Dominant Hollow Knight lore channel (94.6M views, only 93 videos). Owns flagship 'complete lore' topics but uploads slowly — long-tail topics uncovered. (channels.list)
ATTAINABILITY PROOF: channel created 2025-08-27 (Silksong launch window), 21 videos, 1,909,760 total views, multiple 350k+ view videos. A solo newcomer succeeding in months. (channels.list)
5.5k subs, 2.09M total views — second independent proof that tiny channels get large views here. (channels.list)
Multi-game lore channel; two Silksong videos at 275k and 478k views. (channels.list + videos.list)

candidates.monetization_notes: Lore audiences are the strongest Patreon converters in gaming (mossbag/VaatiVidya model — inference from their public Patreon presence). 15min+ docs enable midrolls; gaming CPM moderate. Sea of Sorrow coverage in 2026 is a subscriber-acquisition event.
candidates.production_complexity: Medium: requires completing the game and deep wiki/item-text research per video; footage capture is easy; one quality video/week solo is realistic. Well depth: Silksong alone supports 50+ (characters, areas, endings, item lore, theories, expansion), adjacent indies push it well past 100.
candidates.risks: Single-franchise concentration until multi-game expansion lands; mossbag soaks up the biggest topics; lore demand is wave-shaped (spikes at releases, decays between) — the 2026 expansion mitigates near-term. Fan communities detect low-effort AI scripting quickly.
candidates.originality_defense: Original theory synthesis, cross-referenced primary text (in-game item descriptions), self-captured footage. Analysis and argumentation, definitionally not compilation.

candidates.name: Postmortem (rise-and-fall business documentaries on games & studios)
candidates.niche: Deeply researched 'why this game/studio/franchise died' business documentaries — timelines, financials, design missteps — for the 2024-2026 wave of shutdowns and the huge evergreen back catalog
candidates.format: 20-40 min documentary: original timeline reconstruction from cited reporting, own motion graphics/charts, transformative fair-use footage, human-written script + AI narration acceptable
candidates.why_now: The industry's 2024-2026 contraction (live-service shutdowns, studio closures) generates a constant stream of fresh subjects on top of hundreds of evergreen ones. The format is proven to be TOPIC-driven, not channel-driven: a 21.9k-sub channel with only 11 uploads has a 749k-view rise-and-fall documentary (YouTube API verified).

demand_evidence.title: PUBG Mobile: The Rise and Fall of an Empire (Glad2be1000)
demand_evidence.finding: 749,005 views on a channel with 21,900 subs and just 11 videos — 34x views-to-subs ratio proves click demand independent of channel size (YouTube API)

demand_evidence.title: GVMERS channel
demand_evidence.finding: 541,000 subs, 73M views across only 168 documentary videos = ~435k avg views/video; self-described 4-person team, so format is near-solo-producible (YouTube API channels.list, retrieved 2026-07-12)
nerdSlayer's 'Death of a Game' and GVMERS repeatedly recommended by communities — established, named audience appetite for the genre (search snippet, community source)

competitor_scan.notes: Genre leader; 73M views / 168 videos; slow cadence (4-person team, ~13 yrs) leaves hundreds of subjects uncovered. (channels.list)
ATTAINABILITY PROOF: 11 videos, 4.54M total views, 749k on one rise-and-fall doc. (channels.list + videos.list)
Long-running 'Death of a Game' series; not API-verified this session (search.list quota exhausted; handle uncertain) — treat size as unverified.

candidates.monetization_notes: Long runtimes = multiple midrolls; business/industry framing attracts finance-adjacent advertisers (inference). Back-catalog is highly evergreen — dead games stay dead. Sponsor-friendly (VPN/game services).
candidates.production_complexity: High — the hardest of the four: each video needs days of research across news archives, earnings reports, dev interviews. Solo cadence realistically 2/month. Well depth effectively unlimited (500+ dead games/studios/franchises).
candidates.risks: Highest reused-content exposure of the four: footage-heavy docs must lead with original graphics, charts, and analysis to survive YPP review (mitigable, but real). Research errors on contested shutdowns invite community backlash. Slow cadence delays monetization threshold.
candidates.originality_defense: Value is the original research synthesis: sourced timelines, financial analysis, original motion graphics. Footage used as illustrative evidence under commentary, never as the content itself — structurally the opposite of a compilation.

candidates.name: Joker Math (Balatro & roguelike-deckbuilder strategy/probability explainers)
candidates.niche: Strategy, scoring-math, and design analysis for Balatro and the roguelike-deckbuilder genre (Slay the Spire, Monster Train 2, new releases)
candidates.format: 8-15 min screen-capture explainers with score-math overlays: deck/joker analysis, probability breakdowns, 'why this build works' — AI narration viable, original math is the product
candidates.why_now: Balatro's free 1.1 update — the game's first content expansion — lands in 2026 on all platforms (confirmed still in active development Feb 2026). Every joker/mechanic it adds resets the strategy meta and search demand. Meanwhile a channel created Feb 2025 has already amassed 21.8M views in this niche, proving late entry still works.

ATTAINABILITY PROOF: created 2025-02-01, 30.6k subs, 21.8M total views in ~17 months (heavy Shorts mix — inference from views/subs ratio). (channels.list)
Multiple sub-10k-view strategy videos exist — the floor is real; differentiation on math rigor required. (videos.list)

candidates.monetization_notes: Weakest CPM story of the four (younger casual audience, shorter videos — inference). Compensations: very low production cost per video, Shorts funnel demonstrably works here (Roze), genre expansion adds sponsor surface (new deckbuilder launches).
candidates.production_complexity: Low — easiest of the four: screen capture + overlay math + script. High cadence (3+/week) feasible solo. Well: ~150 jokers x builds, deck strategies, challenge runs, probability theory, plus genre-wide coverage → 100+ videos comfortably, more after 1.1.
candidates.risks: Single-game concentration until genre expansion; two incumbents (Balatro University, Roze) own recommendation mindshare; if 1.1 slips past 2026 the demand-reset thesis delays ('done when it's done' per developer). Balatro-only demand is post-peak — API data shows it persists but the explosive 2024 wave is over.
candidates.originality_defense: Original probability math, tested builds, tier analysis from own runs — self-captured footage, analysis-first scripting. Not a compilation by construction.
